header:
Date: 2027-07-27
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 43 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Redwood Solutions), Claire Ramos (Redwood CSM), Jordan Wu (Orion Eng Lead), Maria Lopez (Orion Product), Tim Reynolds (Orion CTO), Sanjay Patel (Orion SRE)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on model selection and version pinning. Reviewed recent eval results comparing redwood-large-1 (v2027-06-15) vs rw-13b-quant and a small reference against public models. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, fallback/rollback policies, and next steps for load testing and infra alignment.
topics: Model evaluation summary: quality vs cost
Version pinning strategy and canary rollout
Performance numbers: latency, throughput, token cost
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, model selection, pinning, results review, next steps.
[00:12] Jordan Wu: Thanks Alex, morning. We ran the small regression suite you sent, saw some hallucinations on category mapping.
[00:20] Priya Singh: yeah we saw that in the 7k prompt sweep too; rw-13b-quant had slightly better precision on SKU mapping but redwood-large-1 had fewer token costs and better latency.
[00:33] Maria Lopez: sorry can you repeat the numbers, latency p50/p95?
[00:37] Priya Singh: p50 around 220ms on dedicated nvidia-a100-ish config, p95 ~580ms for redwood-large-1@v2027-06-15 during our 10k request sample. For rw-13b-quant p50 ~320ms p95 ~900ms. these numbers vary with batching and kv cache hit rates.
[01:02] Tim Reynolds: nv-a100? we are evaluating both Dedicated and Hosted right now, if Dedicated hits that p95 it's fine but cost is the concern.
[01:12] Alex Martinez: right, cost per 1k tokens for redwood-large-1 on your Dedicated pilot estimate was around $0.18 after our quantization profile; rw-13b-quant was slightly cheaper per token but needed more concurrency so infra cost rose.
[01:28] Sanjay Patel: our SRE worry is tail latency and how fast rollback is if model degrades. what's Redwood's rollback look like?
[01:34] Priya Singh: we support canary rollouts by version and automated fallback policies. workflow we propose: pin to redwood-large-1@v2027-06-15 as the primary on a small Dedicated pool (20% traffic), observe metrics for 24h, then expand to 100%. If latency/p95 or error-rate rise above thresholds we auto-fallback to rw-13b-quant or a previous v. The rollback is near-instant because we route at the gateway layer.
[02:00] Jordan Wu: are those thresholds configurable? we want to trigger on quality regressions too, not just latency.
[02:06] Priya Singh: yes, you can set SLOs on latency, error-rate, and quality metrics — we integrate with your eval prompt set. If model answers drop below a precision threshold we can divert traffic to fallback model and create an alert.
[02:20] Maria Lopez: how do we measure quality in realtime?
[02:23] Priya Singh: two ways: 1) server-side lightweight classifiers on outputs (we discussed the reranker earlier) and 2) continuous evals on streamed samples using your canonical prompts, both can feed into the rollout policy.
[02:38] Daniel Park: note that prefix/KV cache hit-rate matters a lot; in our benchmarks a 10% increase in cache hit-rate cut p95 by ~150ms for redwood-large-1. so prompt engineering + caching config matter.
[02:50] Jordan Wu: good to know. we saw some noise in our dataset — multiple prompts share long shared prefixes. that should help.
[02:58] Alex Martinez: quick note on quantization: redwood supports multiple quant profiles. rw-13b-quant is using int8-mixed which saved token cost but slightly affected mapping recall in your tests.
[03:12] Tim Reynolds: what about vendor lock? if we pin to redwood-large-1 are we locked for model variants? we still want the ability to move later.
[03:20] Alex Martinez: absolutely not locked. pinning is purely per-route version pin. you can change it anytime, and policies let you schedule automated rollbacks or A/B tests.
[03:31] Maria Lopez: any competitor gaps we should watch for? we compared against OpenAI endpoints for a couple of prompts where reasoning depth mattered, OpenAI was stronger on a handful but cost was ~2-3x.
[03:45] Priya Singh: yeah, Anthropic and some public models like Falcon-40b had better long-form reasoning for our small set but at much higher infra costs and TPU-only constraints. also we saw more token generation in some cases, so cost unpredictability.
[04:00] Jordan Wu: ok focusing on the pin. Priya, you suggested redwood-large-1@v2027-06-15 as candidate. can you summarize why?
[04:08] Priya Singh: sure — balance of latency, quality, and cost. It consistently hit your SKU mapping thresholds in our 10k test set, p50/p95 latency profile is favorable, and it supports our KV/prefix caching and batching knobs that match your workload. rollback path tested and routing is fast.
[04:24] Jordan Wu: do we need to change prompts or can we keep current pipeline?
[04:27] Priya Singh: keep pipeline but we recommend enabling the prefix caching and raising min-batch to 8 for the Dedicated pool; that reduced per-token compute on our runs. we also recommend a lightweight reranker to reduce hallucination on SKU mapping.
[04:40] Sanjay Patel: batch size 8 ok, but network egress could burst; we will confirm firewall rules.
[04:46] Alex Martinez: noted — include that in infra call. also, for the canary, we advise 20% traffic on a 3-node Dedicated pool with burst capacity of 1 extra node.
[04:58] Maria Lopez: what's the expected cost delta if we do that?
[05:02] Alex Martinez: rough estimate, for typical Orion volume, pinned redwood-large-1 Dedicated pilot ~ $18k/month for the reserved pilot footprint, rw-13b-quant alternative ~ $15k/month but with higher concurrency needs which may push ops cost. We'll send an updated SOW with exact numbers.
[05:18] Jordan Wu: can we do a 24-hour stress test that simulates our peak black-friday-like traffic?
[05:22] Priya Singh: yes, Priya will run a 24h test and include reg tests against the canonical prompt set. We'll collect p50/p95, error-rate, cache hit-rate, and quality regression count.
[05:34] Maria Lopez: for quality regressions, what counts as a failure?
[05:37] Priya Singh: we count failures as mis-classifications on SKU mapping, incorrect price/responses, or places where the reranker score drops below 0.7. We'll include examples in the report.
[05:48] Tim Reynolds: about security — we need SOC2 audit docs and KMS details for Dedicated.
[05:54] Alex Martinez: Claire will share our compliance pack after the call, includes SOC 2 Type II summary, KMS/HSM notes, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit log examples.
[06:05] Claire Ramos: I will drop the link in the follow-up email.
[06:09] Jordan Wu: we need to check data residency for EU customers, some of our stores are in EU region.
[06:14] Priya Singh: Redwood supports region pinning, and our Private option can be deployed in your VPC if needed. We'll include region options in the SOW.
[06:24] Daniel Park: small note — when you run the 24h test include KV cache warmup period; the first hour will look worse without warm caches.
[06:34] Jordan Wu: good call. we'll do a warmup phase.
[06:36] Alex Martinez: OK recap: pin candidate redwood-large-1@v2027-06-15, Priya runs 24h load + regression tests, Jordan sends canonical prompts and failing examples, Alex to share pricing/SOW and Claire to send compliance pack. schedule infra deep dive for SREs.
[06:53] Maria Lopez: timeline for going live after canary? if canary passes 24h, how quickly can we ramp?
[06:57] Priya Singh: typically we expand over 48 hours in two steps, monitor the metrics; full ramp could be 72 hours after canary passes, but that's configurable.
[07:06] Jordan Wu: sounds good. any concerns about rollback speed?
[07:09] Priya Singh: rollback is traffic routing change and is near-instant; client-side drains may take short time but nothing long.
[07:17] Alex Martinez: any other questions?
[07:19] Sanjay Patel: we'll validate firewall rules and share before infra call.
[07:22] Jordan Wu: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[07:24] Alex Martinez: great, we'll follow up with notes and links. thanks all.
[07:30] (recording stops)

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-words from auto-transcribe (e.g., "nv-a100-ish" typed from audio), speaker labels sometimes generic in the raw export but cleaned minimally for readability. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.app/s/ORION/poc-model-results-2027-07-26.pdf, Redwood compliance pack (link to be sent), SOW draft (to be shared by Alex).
